speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. Can you describe when the rash first appeared and whether it started on your face or trunk before spreading to your extremities? Also, have you noticed any swollen lymph nodes in your neck or behind your ears?

speaker: Patient
text: 11-year-old girl. The patient has been experiencing a mildly pruritic rash on her trunk and extremities for 2 days. One week ago, she developed symptoms of low-grade fever, rhinorrhea, and headache. A facial rash appeared 4 days later, sparing the perioral area.

speaker: Doctor
text: The description of a facial rash sparing the perioral area followed by a truncal rash is highly suggestive of Erythema Infectiosum, also known as Fifth Disease. To confirm this diagnosis, I need to assess for other specific signs. Have you noticed any joint pain or swelling, and did the facial rash have a "slapped cheek" appearance?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Mildly pruritic rash on trunk and extremities. I also have Low-grade fever, Rhinorrhea, Headache, Facial rash not involving the perioral skin.

speaker: Doctor
text: The clinical presentation is classic for Erythema Infectiosum caused by Parvovirus B19. DIAGNOSIS READY: Erythema Infectiosum (Fifth Disease)
